turns.text: Why did researchers need Batch Normalization, and where were the existing methods getting stuck?
Batch normalization stabilized deep-network training by normalizing intermediate activations during mini-batch learning. It made higher learning rates and deeper networks easier to use in practice.
Activations are centered, scaled, then shifted by learned parameters inside the network.

Experts generally treat batch normalization as a practical training stabilizer, while noting that later architectures sometimes replace it with other normalization methods. Its long-term legacy is making activation statistics an explicit part of deep-network optimization.
